brief: ZeroHedge relays Goldman's Mark Wilson: hedge funds sold global AI stocks for a sixth straight day, pushing the 6-day flow Z-score through -3, the most extreme position cut since ChatGPT launched. Asia, TMT and global long/short funds have given back roughly half their 2026 gains since June. Wilson argues sentiment overshot bearish the way it overshot bullish in Q2, and expects AI leadership to flip from spend beneficiaries to the biggest AI investors, who can self-fund capex and show ROI through Q3 earnings, because no evidence of slowing compute demand has emerged. Two catalysts drove the week: a CoreWeave co-founder's comment that life insurers offer "unlimited" capital for AI, and a sharpening debate over frontier-lab economics and credit quality. CoreWeave stock fell 15% and its CDS hit a record. Wilson calls the bond market's break lower in yields more significant than equity moves, consistent with Goldman's Monday upgrade of bonds to Overweight, though oil near $100 complicates that read. ZeroHedge counters: positioning can mean-revert, but funding costs can't, so any AI-winners bounce is a positioning trade until CoreWeave's bondholders say otherwise, with Meta's October 21 earnings as the next test.
